title: Haystack Block Reduction with Nonuniform Randomness
summary: The converse block-size reduction holds for uniform encoding output; it remains open for nonuniform randomness and requires identifying when padding noise has a suitable distribution.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether an attack on a one-block Haystack cipher can be reduced to an attack on a parallel $b$-block Haystack cipher when the randomness $r$ is nonuniformly distributed, and characterize the distributional conditions under which the reduction succeeds. The candidate approach pads each one-block query arbitrarily to $b$ blocks and treats the irrelevant ciphertext blocks as noise. The unresolved obstacle is that this noise may not match the distribution of the bits of $r$ expected by the one-block adversary, potentially preventing its attack.

scope.domain: Security reductions between one-block and parallel multi-block Haystack ciphers.
assumptions: The randomness r is nonuniformly distributed.
parameters: b: the number of blocks in the parallel Haystack cipher
r: the randomness whose bit distribution may differ from the padding noise
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether a one-block attack reduces to the parallel b-block setting under nonuniform randomness, and which distributional conditions make the reduction succeed.

citations.label: Haystack ciphers : White-box countermeasures as Symmetric encryption

progress.summary: The source proposes padding each one-block query to b blocks and treating the irrelevant ciphertext blocks as noise. It leaves open whether this works when that noise differs from the distribution expected by the one-block adversary.
